articles.title: oPt: UNRWA Situation Report #231 on the Humanitarian Crisis in the Gaza Strip and the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem) [EN/AR]
articles.description: Country: occupied Palestinian territory Source: UN Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East Please refer to the attached files. All information updated for 15 - 28 July 2026 [1] Days 1011 - 1024 since the start of the war in the Gaza Strip Highlights The Gaza Strip UNRWA summer learning activities started on 18 July, with 39,509 children (21,666 girls, 17,843 boys, including 875 children with disabilities) participating between 20 and 26 July. Summer activities also started at the UNRWA Rehabilitation Centre for the Visually Impaired (RCVI). On 21 July, UNRWA resumed operations at Beach Camp Health Centre in western Gaza City, which had been closed since sustaining damage during the September-October 2025 military escalation. On 29 July, UNRWA also opened the Bahrain Medical Point, in southern Gaza City. Together, the two facilities are expected to serve a large catchment area (almost 100,000 people), expanding access to essential primary healthcare services across densely populated areas of Gaza City. The operating environment in Gaza continues to deteriorate, with a significant escalation in hostilities observed in the humanitarian area – also known as the “green zone” – west of the so-called “yellow line” of control designated by Israeli forces. There have also been additional advances of the yellow line across multiple areas, including in eastern Middle Area, Gaza City and Khan Younis. Multiple evacuation orders and shelter-in place orders were issued over the past week with several humanitarian infrastructure affected (including more than ten UNRWA premises). Restrictions on the entry of lubricant oil and spare parts continue to pose a critical challenge for humanitarian operation, More than half of UNRWA’s fleet is no longer operational due to the shortage of engine oil and spare parts. In addition, 62 water wells have been affected by fuel and lubricant shortages, leading to a reduction of 42 percent in UNRWA’s production and distribution of clean water. The occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem On 27 July, the UNRWA Kalandia Training Centre in East Jerusalem was subject to an unauthorised entry by Israeli forces and Jerusalem Municipality officials, during which they inspected the premises while educational activities were ongoing. As a United Nations property, the Kalandia Training Centre is protected under international law.

articles.title: 'Worst case scenario' likely as ships trapped by Trump's war could spur 'super spreader'
articles.description: Stalled ships near the Strait of Hormuz amid President Donald Trump 's Iran war threaten more than just oil markets as scientists warn idling vessels could trigger an invasive species "super-spreader event," according to reports on Tuesday. More than 1,500 ships have sat idle in the trade channel since the conflict began on Feb. 28 and experts revealed that organisms growing on hulls and hitchhiking on the vessels could devastate global ecosystems once trade resumes, USA Today reported. "If you had to sort of design a worst-case scenario, it would look a lot like this," Mario Tamburri, a professor at the University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science and the study’s lead author, told USA Today. "It’s a perfect storm." When ships don't move for days or weeks, microbes, algae and other marine organisms can colonize the submerged parts of the vessel. Experts warned that after 10 days these organisms can hit the "rapid growth phase." "These organisms, when introduced to other ecosystems, can cause a wide array of consequences, from outcompeting native species to damaging infrastructure to introducing pathogens harmful to marine life and, sometimes, humans," according to USA Today. Tamburri called the situation unprecedented, adding that the high number of ships, estimated at about 1,500 vessels sitting along the trade route, could harbor "organisms that thrive in the Middle East waters, such as the Strait of Hormuz, Gulf of Oman and Persian Gulf." The organisms can adapt to areas that see extreme seasonal changes. Areas most at-risk for spreading these colonizers are near the strait and with similar high salinity and high temperature conditions, including ports in Southeast Asia and India. These are at higher risk compared to other locations, Tamburri said. He cautioned Singapore, an international hub for commercial shipping, could be a high risk. "Those organisms can withstand extremes," Tamburri said. "They’re tolerant organisms, which makes them good candidates for invasions when they go to a new location."

articles.title: 'Heckuva job Pete!' Firestorm for Trump admin as 'huge problem' exposed in Iran war
articles.description: The U.S. Army has used up nearly all of its stockpile of long-range, precision surface-to-surface missiles during five months of war with Iran — a depletion that hasn't been previously reported and is raising concerns about military readiness. The weapons in question are Army Tactical Missile Systems and the newer Precision Strike Missiles, which cost more than $1 million apiece and allow accurate strikes from a safe distance, three sources told Reuters . Two sources said "virtually all" of these munitions have been used. ATACMS have also been central to Ukraine's ability to strike targets inside Russia, and analysts consider both systems important for any future conflict with China. A fourth source said Central Command has nearly exhausted its pre-war supply but has been able to reload from stocks elsewhere in the U.S. military. The 80-year-old president insists the U.S. has far more munitions than anyone in the world, but critics pointed to the report as another example of his failures since launching the war in February. "Heckuva job Petey! @SecWar ," cracked The Bulwark's Tim Miller. "All you need to know about 'grand strategy' in this administration," muttered German journalist Joerg Lau. "It’s not quite right to say the Trump regime used up virtually all of America’s best missiles in the war on Iran this year, only to gain nothing (in fact, to lose valuable things)," said international relations professor Nicholas Grossman. "Because the Trump regime used up someone of America’s best missiles in a war in Yemen last year, only to gain nothing." "That PrSM is low is no surprise because the production just began. But no one should pretend that the combined depletion of ATACMS/PrSM is not a huge problem," warned Tom Karako, director of the Missile Defense Project at the Center for Strategic and International Studies. "Exactly what we warned against for months!!!" shouted global affairs columnist Richard Heydarian. "The thing is though their military was totally destroyed for 1000 years," joked columnist Jeb Lund.

articles.title: Trump Hit by Fox Poll Shocker that Undercuts His Latest Midterm Tirade
articles.description: On Monday, CNN analyst Harry Enten flagged a truly surprising finding in a Fox News poll that had eluded our attention: Trump’s approval is nine points underwater in very red Texas , which he won by 14 points in 2024. That’s not all: The Fox poll, which shows Democrat James Talarico up by three points, finds Trump’s approval at an astounding 18 percent among independents in Texas, with 50 percent disapproving strongly . That’s remarkable, especially given how key independents are in Texas races. All this comes as Trump unleashed a long tirade claiming “my REAL poll numbers” are “the best they have ever been.” Trump also bizarrely listed a long litany of accomplishments that were, well, entirely made up, showing he has zero intention to help his party by recalibrating. We talked to Democratic strategist Sawyer Hacket, who knows Texas and has worked on midterms. He explains why Trump’s standing with Texas independents is “absolutely shocking,” what the path to victory there looks like, where Talarico still must improve, and how numbers like these could open up other red states for Democrats. Listen to this episode here .
